PullRequest.Title: sessions: Get Started checklist for new Agents window users
PullRequest.Body:

Most new users of the Agents window come from Copilot Chat in the editor, and almost 9 in 10 title bar users don't send a request within 24 hours. This adds a **Get Started** checklist to the Sessions view. It shows everything the window can do up front without blocking anyone, and ticks items off as users do them, like the checklists in Linear and Asana.

### What

- **Experiment setting** `sessions.getStarted.checklist` (`tags: ['experimental']`, `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`): `none` (default, control), `aboveSessions`, `belowSessions`.
- **Who sees it:** users who had created fewer than 2 sessions in the Agents window when they first see the Sessions view. This is decided once and stored per machine. It needs AI features, sign-in and the desktop layout. It waits until no onboarding tour has shown for a moment, so it never overlaps the new-session tour.
- **Items:** each completes automatically and stays complete.

| Item | Completes when | Show Me tour |
|---|---|---|
| Start a session | A session is created | Chat input → project picker |
| Run two agents at once | Two sessions run at the same time | New → isolation picker (New Worktree vs. Branch) → chat input |
| Work in a second project | Sessions exist in two projects, grouped like the sessions list | The user's project in the sessions list ("You've worked in **x** from this window") → project picker, opened, suggesting recent editor projects |
| Review and keep changes | A merge, commit or pull request starts | Opens a session with changes → changes pill → diff editor → keep actions |
| Set up an automation | An automation exists | Automations → example templates → Create Automation |

- **Card:** progress ("2 of 5"), collapse to one line, expand and collapse items, and Hide (until restart) or Don't Show Again. **Agents: Show Getting Started Checklist** brings it back. Completing an item gives a quiet highlight and a screen reader announcement. When everything is done, it says "You're all set" and then goes away.
- **Accessibility:** list semantics with done and not done states, roving keyboard navigation, Escape back to the sessions list, accessibility help with a verbosity setting (`accessibility.verbosity.sessionsGetStarted`), design tokens only, and all themes including high contrast.
- **Telemetry:**
  - `experimentTrigger` in every arm, when an eligible user first sees the place of the checklist.
  - `onboarding.getStartedChecklistItemCompleted` in every arm, for eligible users.
  - `onboarding.getStartedChecklistAction` (shown, Show Me, collapse, expand, hide, dismiss, restore) in the treatment.
  - Nothing is logged in developer-mode previews.
- **Supporting changes:**
  - `isPresenting` on the onboarding service.
  - Spotlight targets for the Automations entry, templates and Create button, the workspace section headers, the changes pill, the changes actions and the new-session input.
  - Top and bottom notice slots in the Sessions view.

### How to test

1. Set `"sessions.getStarted.checklist": "aboveSessions"` (or `"belowSessions"`).
2. Use a fresh user data dir. To preview with an existing profile, also set `"onboarding.developerMode": { "sessions.getStarted.checklist": true }`.
3. Open the Agents window. The checklist shows above (or below) the sessions list.
4. Try each **Show Me**. Then start sessions, use a second project, merge changes and create an automation to tick the items off.
5. Hide it, or choose Don't Show Again, then run **Agents: Show Getting Started Checklist**.

### Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/getStarted/test/common/getStartedChecklist.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/getStarted/test/browser/getStartedChecklistService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/getStarted/test/browser/getStartedChecklistWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/getStarted/test/browser/getStartedTours.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/getStarted/test/browser/getStartedTourRunner.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListNotice.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsViewPane.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/automationsView.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/onboarding/test/browser/onboardingService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatInputPills.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatInput.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatUserInteraction.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/test/browser/changesViewActions.test.ts`: passed (508 tests)
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `./node_modules/.bin/eslint <changed .ts files>`: passed, no warnings
- `node build/stylelint.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/getStarted/browser/media/getStartedChecklist.css src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/media/sessionsViewPane.css`: passed
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- Component fixtures `sessions/getStarted/*` (26 variants, including both placements and high contrast) render without errors.
- Tried end to end in Code OSS with real agents. Every item completed through its real flow, and every Show Me step showed its control.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed scan, its lifetime subscription, and the provider's per-adapter refresh behavior are directly traced. Exact milliseconds depend on catalogue size and provider mix, which is reflected in medium severity rather than uncertainty about the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and observable subscriptions across every retained session
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each subscribed status, archive, workspace, quick-chat, or automation mutation reruns an O(N) scan of all sessions; a provider refresh/reconnect that updates N cached adapters separately can therefore perform O(N²) property reads. The agent-host cache persists up to 100 sessions per host and the merged catalogue spans providers, so N is realistically large for long-lived users.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased renderer CPU/GC pressure and delayed Agents-window updates during session catalogue refreshes or bursts of session state transitions.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, checklist tracking did not exist, so session mutations and provider refreshes did not trigger this additional collection-wide scan or attach these per-session observable dependencies.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new derived signal loops over the merged session catalogue and reads several mutable observables from every session. Once eligibility is true, the model's lifetime autorun continuously reads this signal, including after the checklist is dismissed or all items are complete and the card can never render again.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 169-181 add the full-session loop and per-session observable reads; RIGHT line 163 introduces the merged-session source consumed by that loop. This entire tracking path is new in the PR.
Findings.Title: Avoid full-catalogue rescans from per-session observables
Findings.Impact: An initially eligible user who later accumulates many sessions can pay repeated full-catalogue scans for the rest of the window lifetime; host reconnects/full refreshes are the strongest trigger because cached adapters are updated one by one. This can produce avoidable CPU spikes and UI latency even after the checklist has disappeared permanently.
Findings.Evidence: The added loop reads `isAutomation`, `status`, `isArchived`, `workspace`, and `isQuickChat` with the same observable reader for every element. `GetStartedChecklistModel`'s autorun reads `_signals` whenever `state.eligible === true` and has no completed/dismissed stop condition, while `visible` merely hides the card when `allDone`. In `BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider._refreshSessions`, cached adapters are updated inside a loop and the aggregate `onDidChangeSessions` event is emitted only afterward, so those child-observable writes can invalidate this scan once per adapter rather than once per refresh.
Findings.Recommendation: Drive the calculation from the coalesced `onDidChangeSessions` event using untracked per-session snapshots, or maintain incremental counts from the event's added/removed/changed sets. Also stop observing each signal once its corresponding item is latched complete (and stop all session observation once the session-backed items are complete), while retaining only the automation/changes observers still needed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Agents window and reveal the Sessions view for the first time in the control or treatment arm
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workbench restoration, entitlement resolution, Sessions-view visibility, and onboarding-idle state must complete; the checklist then waits 1.5 seconds before deciding eligibility. The AfterRestored contribution constructs the service off the initial restore critical path, and telemetry/storage writes do not block rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potentially initiate an agent-host `listSessions()` refresh through a cold provider cache when the new signal first calls `getSessions()`
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight refresh per cold agent-host provider; warm caches add no call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Sessions view already queried the same provider catalogue; this PR adds another consumer but existing provider in-flight/cache guards coalesce cold loading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The call returns cached sessions synchronously and does not await the network refresh, so it is off the checklist reveal critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and write machine-local eligibility/progress state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read at model construction, one eligibility write, then at most one write per completion/collapse/dismiss/restore action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small fixed-size storage values; eligibility state is synchronously committed before visibility updates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One experiment trigger, up to five completion events, and bounded user-action events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These checklist telemetry events did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Telemetry dispatch is not awaited and is off the UI critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Merged sessions from all registered providers; cold agent-host caches can contain up to 100 persisted entries per host and live listings are not capped to that value. Eligibility itself is a one-time decision.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Readiness is one autorun with a disposable timeout. Provider session cache loads use their existing in-flight/backoff coalescing, and no new parallel per-session boundary burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Application storage reads are warm synchronous service reads. `getSessions()` returns provider caches immediately; on a cold agent-host cache it can start the provider's existing single coalesced `listSessions()` refresh asynchronously. Automation catalogues remain owned/cached by their providers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: service construction, readiness gating, cache behavior, and boundary placement are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold provider state and catalogue size vary, but the new boundary calls are cached/coalesced and not awaited; no boundary-fanout finding is warranted.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. Eager service construction is AfterRestored, dependencies are already eager or lightweight/cached, and cold provider work is coalesced and off the reveal critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Track checklist completion while sessions are created, run, archived, refreshed, or reconnected
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider/session observable mutations synchronously invalidate the checklist signal before the renderer can settle; completed items then write storage and queue telemetry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive existing provider session catalogue/summary notifications
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing host refresh/notification stream; a full refresh can update N adapters before one aggregate event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider updates occurred without checklist-wide rescans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Network receipt is pre-existing, but the diff adds synchronous O(N) CPU work to each child-observable mutation caused by it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most five completion writes over the checklist lifetime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fixed and bounded; not the reported scaling mechanism.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All merged sessions N, including archived sessions and sessions retained by multiple providers; provider refreshes can mutate N cached adapters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable recomputation is synchronous on the renderer. Provider notifications are debounced at the aggregate event layer, but the added derived reads subscribe directly to each adapter's child observables, bypassing that coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The session array is cached by `observableFromEvent`, but every recomputation rescans it and re-reads mutable child observables. Completion state is latched in storage, yet the signal remains observed after dismissal/all-done.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added per-session observable reads, lifetime autorun, all-done visibility behavior, and provider per-adapter refresh loop are directly present.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on provider count, retained session count, and refresh cadence; the O(N) per mutation and O(N²) full-refresh mechanism are established, so uncertainty affects severity only.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression submitted: full-catalogue scans remain active for eligible users, including after the checklist can no longer render.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render, expand, collapse, complete, hide, or dismiss the checklist card
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each state change rebuilds at most five checklist rows, emits a height event, and synchronously relayouts the Sessions sidebar split view.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed checklist cardinality of four or five items; completion animation adds one timer per newly completed item, capped at five.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM work is synchronous and user/event driven. Completion timers are independent but bounded; widget disposal owns timers and render disposables.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No external cache. Render listeners and hover instances are replaced through a MutableDisposable store, and the widget is disposed when hidden or moved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: widget reconstruction, timer ownership, and relayout calls are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sidebar layout cost depends on DOM/theme state, but invocation count is fixed and low.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The synchronous layout work is bounded to a five-row card and infrequent state changes, with cleanup ownership intact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run a checklist “Show Me” tour for sessions, projects, changes, or automations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tour runner snapshots/sorts sessions, optionally waits up to two seconds for recent-project history, then the onboarding sequencer opens the required view/session/editor step by step.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load/resolve recent VS Code folders and up to ten workspace files through SessionsRecentWorkspacesService
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached history load, capped at ten workspace files; the tour consumes the cached result and returns at most two labels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Get Started tour did not consume recent-project history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the second-project tour may wait, capped at two seconds; this is a user-invoked explanatory flow, not startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open at most one existing session, which may hydrate provider-owned session details
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one session open for the keep-changes tour, skipped when already active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No checklist tour opened a session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the selected tour's step critical path and intentionally awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the existing View Session Changes command to resolve/show diffs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command invocation, skipped when the correct changes editor is already visible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No checklist tour invoked the existing command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the user-requested changes-tour step; no per-file command fan-out is added by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user-selected tour at a time; session snapshot scales with N, recent workspace history is capped to ten own and ten VS Code entries, and only two project labels are retained.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The onboarding service serializes scenarios globally. Repeating the same item joins the current promise; selecting another cancels and disposes the previous run, so no concurrent tour burst occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Recent workspace history is preloaded/cached by its service and bounded; a loading history wait times out after two seconds. Session and automation catalogues use existing provider caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: cancellation, sequencing, caps, timeouts, and call cardinalities are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider session hydration and diff resolution duration vary, but calls are user requested, single-cardinality, sequenced, and skipped when already satisfied.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Boundary work is bounded, intentional, and only on the user-invoked tour path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Queue onboarding scenarios and render the new spotlight targets in sessions, changes, chat pills, and automations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Queue mutations update one boolean observable; renderers add/remove a data attribute and weak-map entry. Target lookup/style geometry occurs only while a tour resolves a step.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One marker per rendered target element/section/pill; tour target lookup happens per bounded tour step.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The onboarding queue is serialized, and marker registrations are disposed with their renderer/widget stores.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Registrations use a WeakMap and renderer-scoped disposables, so removed DOM elements are not retained by the new markers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: marker implementation is a setAttribute/WeakMap registration with disposal, and queue updates are constant-time.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM target count varies with rendered rows, but marking is constant work per rendered element and no global observer is added.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Added target metadata does not change boundary frequency or create unbounded retention.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 32 changed files and relevant transitive services. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity repeated-work finding for lifetime per-session observable tracking that can turn provider refreshes into quadratic catalogue scans. Startup/service construction, widget relayout, target registration, telemetry/storage, and Show Me boundary calls were traced and found bounded, cached/coalesced, disposed, or explicitly user-invoked.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
